scenarios.title: The benchmark score ends the discussion
scenarios.prompt: A team prefers a new platform and highlights its strong benchmark score. It dismisses workload, data quality and operating constraints that are not measured by the benchmark.
scenarios.question: What should a red-team review ask?

options.text: Which important failure modes and decision criteria are not represented by the score?
How can the score be presented more prominently to the steering committee?
Which competing platform has the weakest marketing material?

scenarios.explanation: The preferred conclusion is selecting supportive evidence. A red-team review tests what the benchmark omits and whether the score transfers to the real operating context.
missingEvidence: Definition and construction of the benchmark.
Performance under the organisation’s workload and data.
Important outcomes not represented by the score.
scenarios.evidenceNote: Confirmation bias is a plausible lens because evidence outside the preferred score is discounted. The benchmark may still be highly informative when it matches the decision goal.
scenarios.nextAction: List the benchmark’s blind spots and test the two most consequential ones.

scenarios.title: A good KPI excuses a weak process
scenarios.prompt: A support team meets its response-time KPI by closing tickets early and reopening them later. Leaders call the process successful because the dashboard is green.
scenarios.question: What should be reviewed separately?

options.text: The measured score, the underlying customer outcome and the process used to produce the score.
Only the dashboard because formal KPIs define success.
Whether the team feels proud of the result.

scenarios.explanation: A favourable measured outcome can hide a poor decision process and a weak real-world outcome. A decision record preserves why the KPI was chosen and what it was meant to represent.
missingEvidence: How ticket handling affects the metric.
The original purpose and known limits of the KPI.
scenarios.evidenceNote: Outcome bias is a useful lens for treating a green result as proof of process quality. Metric design and incentives are also structural causes that require direct analysis.
scenarios.nextAction: Review the KPI, underlying outcome and process as three separate evidence columns.
